title: Hint-Informed Self-Distillation for Reasoning Segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2611.14931v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Reasoning segmentation requires identifying the target referred to by a query among visually similar objects, yet trajectory-level rewards cannot directly indicate which tokens provide relevant visual evidence. We propose Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), which uses target-disambiguation evidence for token-level credit assignment. An external model generates Segment Hints offline from training images, queries, and ground-truth target annotations, organizing target identity, discriminative attributes, confusable objects, and anchoring paths. A hint-conditioned exponential moving average teacher scores the student's own trajectories, and HISD computes the teacher-to-student evidence ratio over a token support set to adjust only the magnitudes of positive group-relative advantages, leaving nonpositive advantages unchanged. translated_title: 面向推理分割的提示信息自蒸馏方法
translated_abstract: 推理分割需要在视觉相似的物体中识别查询所指的目标，然而轨迹级别的奖励无法直接指示哪些标记提供了相关的视觉证据。我们提出了提示信息自蒸馏（HISD），该方法利用目标消歧证据进行标记级别的信用分配。外部模型从训练图像、查询和真实目标标注中离线生成分割提示，组织目标身份、判别性属性、易混淆物体和锚定路径等信息。一个以提示为条件的指数移动平均教师模型对学生自身的推理轨迹进行评分，HISD 在标记支持集上计算教师到学生的证据比率，仅调整正的组相对优势的幅度，而保持非正的优势不变。这种设计在保留目标消歧所需信息的同时，鼓励模型进行简洁的推理。
tldr: 提出提示信息自蒸馏方法HISD，通过外部模型离线生成分割提示，并利用教师-学生证据比率进行标记级别的信用分配，在鼓励简洁推理的同时保留目标消歧所需的关键视觉证据。
en_tdlr: Proposes Hint-Informed Self-Distillation (HISD), which generates segment hints offline via an external model and applies teacher-to-student evidence ratios for token-level credit assignment, encouraging concise reasoning while preserving the visual evidence needed for target disambiguation.
